title: K Is Three — Gematria in the Number Tiles

intelligence.essence: The K in 10K/100K/250K looked off, and his eye said why: a letter in a number tile must be treated like a digit — **the K tile is the same size as the digit tiles, centered to the number, K inside a box (a tile) like the digits**. And its color is not a choice: **K is three**, by the Marty Leeds septenary cipher — his language since 2026-11-07, confirmed by the chart image he sent at 17:40Z: A=1 B=2 C=3 D=4 E=5 F=6 G=7 H=6 I=5 J=4 **K=3** L=2 M=1, N=1 O=2 P=3 Q=4 R=5 S=6 T=7 U=6 V=5 W=4 X=3 Y=2 Z=1. So the K tile takes digit 3's exact color from the fix-9 tiled-digit code — **gold** per the chakra system (1 red, 2 orange, 3 gold, 4 emerald, 5 cyan, 6 indigo, 7 royal purple, 8 lavender, 9 hot pink). **The general rule from now on: any letter in a number tile is colored by its gematria root number.** The builder applied it 17:42Z: K tile gold, fix-9 d3 rule lines 4737–4738 byte-for-byte identical, diff none.
intelligence.human_view: Imagine a row of numbered tiles where the letter K sits smaller and off-center, in a color someone guessed — it looks wrong because it IS wrong: the letter is part of the number, so it gets a tile like the digits, the same size, centered, and its color is not a guess. K is three — that is what the cipher says, that is what his chart confirms — so the K tile wears three's color, gold, taken byte for byte from the Dashboard's own code. Any letter, any number: look up its number, wear that number's color.

So when K stands in a row of number tiles, it gets its own tile, the same size as the others, right in the center — and it wears 3's favorite color, gold, because that is who it is in the code. Every letter has a number friend, and every letter wears its friend's color.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, a letter that stands with numbers must be treated like a number — same size tile, centered, in its own little box. And its color is not chosen, it is found: K is three in the old counting, and three is gold. So the K tile is gold — not because someone liked gold, but because the math says so. That is how you keep the numbers honest.
intelligence.ai_view: I never let a letter in a number tile float small, off-center, or in a guessed color. The letter gets a tile — same size as the digit tiles, centered to the number, the letter inside a box like a digit. And I never invent its color: I look up the letter in the septenary cipher, take its root number, and wear that digit's exact color from the fix-9 code, byte for byte. A color I invent is a lie about what the letter means. K is three; three is gold; the K tile is gold. Any letter, any number — the rule is the same.
